newsitem.title: GERMANY: IBIS DAX index ends share trade at higher levels.
newsitem.headline: IBIS DAX index ends share trade at higher levels.

text.p: Germany's IBIS DAX index ended the day just shy of the key 3,400-point level on Thursday, underpinned by the stronger dollar, upbeat German inflation figures and a firm opening on Wall Street.

The IBIS DAX index, which gauges electronic trade in German shares, ended at 3,396.49, up 29.62 points or 0.88 percent, off earlier highs, while the June DAX DTB future contract ended up 34 points at 3,404.
Earlier the DAX index of bourse trade ended at 3,397.36 points, up 1.41 points or 0.04 percent.

"The main factors today have been the stronger dollar, the well-maintained future and the decent CPI numbers. People are treating with Wall Street almost with contempt at the moment, going with it to a lesser extent than before," a trader said.

The Dow Jones went nearly one percentage point higher at 6,872.93 points early on and while the German market was not tracking its course as slavishly as it has done in the past, the Dow rise did underpin trade.
"The market has done well without huge volumes -- we are seeing bull market indices without bull market volumes," the trader said.
Electronics group Siemens AG was one of the main features in afternoon trade, ending up 2.45 marks at 90.45 marks, recouping some of the losses seen over previous days.
Utility Veba AG was lower over the day, ending down 56 pfennigs at 93.30 marks. Dealers said there was little fundamental information moving the share.
"With Veba it seems to be just a question of more supply than demand," a trader said.

Drugs group Schering was also lower, down 2.20 marks at 162.40 marks after a decision by the European Patent Office to revoke a patent issued to another German group for the treatment of multiple sclerosis.
Schering said it was not affected by the move, but the news impacted on sentiment in pharmaceutical shares.
"For the rest of the week I can see us going nowhere. I suppose if Wall Street is well maintained we could see support there and hold at around these levels," said a trader.
